The Betances is a supportive housing site designed specifically for adults over the age of 55 years old who have a history of homelessness.

Grounded in CUCS’s mission and values, the Program Director ensures the delivery of high quality, trauma\-informed, person\-centered, and culturally responsive services that meet both client needs and funder expectations.



This role requires a result\-driven and equity focused leader with strong clinical and operational expertise, sound judgment, and the ability to lead in complex, highly regulated, and unionized environments. The Program Director builds and supports high performing teams, ensures compliance with regulatory and contractual requirements, manages program budgets and staffing, and cultivates effective partnerships with funders, community organizations, and government agencies.



As a member of CUCS’s leadership team, the Program Director is accountable for program outcomes, staff performance, and service quality. * Coordinate response to high\-risk incidents (e.g., psychiatric emergencies, housing disruption, overdose).
* Ensure post\-incident debriefing and staff wellness support.
* Escalate critical issues appropriately and in a timely manner in alignment with CUCS policies.

Supervision and Coaching

Performance Management and Development

jobs.description:
**Full job description**

**About Indiana Guardianship Services, Inc.**  
Indiana Guardianship Services, Inc. (IGS) is a nonprofit organization whose mission is to prevent abuse, neglect, and exploitation of incapacitated adults through quality, person\-centered advocacy and guardianship services. We serve individuals who require guardianship support across LaPorte and Porter Counties, advocating for clients' rights, wellbeing, and dignity while helping them navigate complex legal, financial, and healthcare systems with care and professionalism. More on us can be found at www.inguardian.org.

**Executive Director Responsibilities**

* Be proficient in NGA Model Code of Ethics and the Standards of Practice,
* Develop and implement the organization’s policies and procedures, assuring adequate review by the Board of Directors,
* Oversee development of the operating budget and long\-range financial plan, in conjunction with the Board of Directors,
* Oversee negotiations and ensures performance of all contracts, in conjunction with the Board of Directors,
* Hire and supervise management level staff, supporting open discussion and communication across departments to ensure optimal client services and employee satisfaction,
* Develop and maintain cooperative working relationships with the Indiana Department of Health and Human Services and the Judicial Branch,
* Encourage and promote the utilization of the significant talents and experience of the Indiana Guardianship Services, Inc. staff with the goal of meeting the mutual needs of the individual and the organization. Promotes team building and collaboration, along with a culture of trust, empathy, and inclusion,
* Ensure Indiana Guardianship Services, Inc. remains in compliance regarding policies and/or HR practices through consultation with counsel and HR professionals,
* Ensure county compliance with court reports, including ensuring that employees are up to date on court filings,
* Facilitate board meetings, staff meetings, management meetings, and full staff trainings, and
* Share in rotating after hours on\-call responsibility.
* Attend court hearings and provide testimony for assigned clients.
* Participate in interdisciplinary team meetings and client appointments.
* Attend one monthly all\-staff meeting at the Michigan City office.
* Process mail and file documents appropriately.
* Share in rotating after\-hours on\-call responsibility.
* Uphold the NGA Model Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice.

**Qualifications**

* Master's of Social Work (MSW), or related required
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, required
* Demonstrated knowledge of Medicaid, Medicare, Social Security, and major insurance providers (UnitedHealthcare, Anthem, Aetna, etc.), required
* Reliable personal transportation, required
* Must pass a background check per IGS policy and applicable program requirements, required
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; willingness to learn case management software, preferred
* Experience or familiarity working with individuals with intellectual/developmental disabilities (IDD) and/or dementia\-related diagnoses, preferred

**Compensation \& Benefits**

* $60,000\-70,000
* Flexible scheduling and discretionary time off available after 90\-day training period.
* Hybrid schedule with flexibility to manage your workday around field and client obligations (Thursdays required for staff meetings)
* Shared after\-hours on\-call rotation so responsibility is spread across the team and not on any one person.
* This role has an expressed goal of transitioning to full\-time as the Porter County program grows.

**How to Apply**

Apply directly through Indeed, or send your resume and cover letter to: philipbarber77@gmail.com.

Please include a cover letter with your application. Because much of this role involves written communication with courts, insurance providers, families, and other care team members, your cover letter is an important part of how we evaluate candidates. In your cover letter, please address the following:

* Why you are interested in guardianship and advocacy work
* Your experience with Medicaid, Medicare, Social Security, or major insurance systems
* Any experience working with clients with intellectual/developmental disabilities or dementia
* How you manage documentation and deadlines in a fast\-paced environment

Indiana Guardianship Services, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer.

Pay: $60,000\.00 \- $70,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule
* Loan forgiveness

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Michigan City, IN 46360

jobs.title: Executive Director Historic Home Museum
jobs.description:
**About Linden Place**

Linden Place, a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit operated by the Friends of Linden Place is a preeminent example of Federal\-style architecture built in 1810 by George DeWolf. During an era when the sea was America's trading highway the DeWolf family amassed great wealth, much of it through the transatlantic slave trade. When the country outlawed the slave trade DeWolf abandoned Bristol, but subsequent generations made a different contribution to American History. Perhaps the mansion's most famous occupant was Colonel Samuel Pomeroy Colt a DeWolf grandson who founded Industrial Trust Bank and U.S. Rubber. His philanthropy and political influence in Bristol, Rhode Island and beyond was a critical turning point in the town's social history and helped make the region a premier destination for locals and tourists alike. Family descendants occupied the house for 177 years until the Friends of Linden Place assumed ownership in1988\. Today the Mansion is a crossroads of history plays host to significant events throughout the year.

**Position Overview**

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director (ED) is the full\-time leader, visionary force, and chief ambassador of Linden Place. The ED is responsible for short\- and long\-term strategic planning, fundraising, grant writing, financial management, community outreach, and daily operations. Ultimately the ED is responsible for managing and providing leadership within the organization

The Executive Director works closely with the Board, guides active committees, and directly oversees a full\-time Museum Director of Operations, a part\-time Experience Coordinator, part\-time event managers, and a dedicated network of volunteers.

**Core Responsibilities**

**1\. Strategic Leadership \& Operational Management**

* **Organizational Vision:** Partner with the Board of Directors to implement, update, and execute the strategic plan to drive long\-term sustainability and growth.
* **Daily Operations:** Oversee all daily operations, facility management, and staffing requirements. Maintain a strong, motivating work culture for staff, interns, and volunteers.
* **Compliance \& Governance:** Ensure organizational compliance with all state and local laws, contracts, conflict\-of\-interest policies, and nonprofit regulations.

**2\. Fundraising \& Development**

* **Revenue Strategy:** Together with the Development Committee, design and execute robust fundraising strategies, including the membership program, end\-of\-year appeals, **401Gives**, and special campaigns.
* **Donor \& Grant Cultivation:** Identify, cultivate, and retain corporate and individual donors. Research, write, and manage grant applications.
* **Signature Events:** Collaborate with the Gala and Development Committees to oversee key fundraising events, including the annual Gala (April), 4th of July picnic, and fall fundraising events.

**3\. Financial Management**

* **Budgeting:** Collaborate with the Treasurer to create the annual organizational budget and manage spending accordingly.
* **Fiscal Oversight:** Handle accounts payable, accounts receivable, monthly cashflow projections, and financial record\-keeping. Coordinate monthly accounts reconciliation with the bookkeepers and Treasurer.

**4\. Programming \& Event Oversight**

* **Public Programming:** Work alongside the Events and Education Committees to develop and execute an annual programming calendar, including concert and lecture series, exhibitions, Halloween programming, group tours, and field trips.
* **Writers' Residency:** Serve as the primary point of contact and lead administrator for the Linden Place Writers’ Residency.

· **Venue Rentals \& Vendors:** Monitor visitation and sales trends to identify growth opportunities. Serve as the primary contact for the site's caterer and coordinate vendors for private weddings, meetings, and community rentals. Retain overall responsibility for evening and weekend event execution managed by team members.

**5\. Marketing \& Communications**

* **Public Relations:** Serve as the primary spokesperson and ambassador for Linden Place to members, donors, the media, elected officials, and the broader community.
* **Digital \& Print Media:** Oversee all internal and external marketing channels, including website maintenance, social media, newsletters, email marketing, and advertising to increase community engagement and visibility.

**Qualifications \& Prerequisites**

* **Nonprofit Leadership:** Proven experience in a leadership or management role within a nonprofit organization, including successful collaboration with a Board of Directors.
* **Financial Acumen:** Demonstrated experience developing and managing operational budgets, tracking cash flow, and maintaining financial records.
* **Fundraising Expertise:** Proven track record in fundraising strategy, donor cultivation, event leadership, and grant writing/administration.
* **Exceptional Communication:** Outstanding written and public speaking skills, with the ability to represent the institution dynamically to the media and public.
* **Operational Insight:** Experience managing staff, building volunteer programs, overseeing facilities, and coordinating public or private events.
* **Strategic Thinker:** An innovative and inspiring leader capable of turning a strategic vision into actionable operational success.

**Compensation \& Benefits**

We offer a competitive salary and benefits package commensurate with experience and skills.

jobs.description:
**Executive Director – Museum Operations \& Fundraising**

**Finger Lakes Boating Museum \| Hammondsport, New York – Finger Lakes Region**  
**flbm.org**

**Full\-Time, Exempt \| On\-Site**  
**Salary:** $65,000 base salary, plus performance bonuses anticipated based on fundraising results  
**Benefits:** Health insurance, retirement plan, short\-term disability, paid time off and holidays  
**Reports to:** Board of Trustees

**About the Executive Director Role**

The Finger Lakes Boating Museum (FLBM) is seeking an Executive Director to lead the Museum’s operations, nonprofit strategy and fundraising efforts in Hammondsport, New York. This hands\-on leadership role oversees museum operations, fundraising and development, donor relations, grant writing, financial management, capital campaigns, staff and volunteer leadership, community engagement and Board partnership.

As FLBM’s senior leader, the Executive Director will move comfortably between strategy and execution, cultivating relationships with donors, community partners and key stakeholders while leading the Museum’s day\-to\-day operations and helping secure the financial support needed for continued growth.

This is a great opportunity for an experienced nonprofit or museum leader who enjoys building relationships, strengthening organizations and seeing the direct impact of their work.

**About the Museum**

Over the past decade, the Finger Lakes Boating Museum has grown from a traveling exhibit without a permanent home into a vibrant museum featuring six galleries and more than 100 historic boats on display, along with a seasonal tour boat program aboard *The Pat II*, hands\-on educational programming through the FLBM Academy and the Keuka Dragons dragon boat club.

The Museum’s location is an important part of its identity and appeal. It is located in Hammondsport, NY at the southern end of Keuka Lake. This region is the heart of New York’s Finger Lakes \- an area known for natural beauty, wineries, tourism and strong sense of community. The Museum’s campus is itself part of the region’s history, occupying buildings originally constructed by the Taylor Wine Company in 1886\.

**Areas of Responsibility**

**Financial \& Operational Management:** Manage the Museum’s financial resources in accordance with the Board\-approved budget and oversee day\-to\-day museum operations.

**Strategic Leadership:** Partner with the Board of Trustees to develop and execute strategic plans and initiatives that advance FLBM’s mission and long\-term sustainability.

**Staff \& Volunteer Leadership:** Lead Museum staff while supporting, engaging and expanding FLBM’s critical volunteer community.

**Donor \& Community Relations:** Develop strong relationships with major donors, regional business leaders, community partners, public officials and other key stakeholders.

**Fundraising \& Development:** In coordination with the Museum’s Resource Development Committee, serve as the Museum’s focal point for fundraising, building relationships with donors and securing unrestricted operating support and other philanthropic investment.

**Grant Writing:** Sustain and grow grant funding through successful local, state and federal grant development.

**Capital Campaigns:** Work with the Board to plan and lead capital campaign initiatives.

**Marketing \& Visibility:** Strengthen the Museum’s community presence, public relations, marketing and social media visibility.

**Facilities \& Vendor Oversight:** Coordinate Museum maintenance priorities and oversee vendor and contract performance for projects across the FLBM campus.

**What We’re Looking For**

The successful candidate will be a strong relationship builder and strategic leader who is equally comfortable representing the Museum externally and managing the organization internally.

Successful candidates will have:

An Associate degree (2\-year) and at least three years of senior\-level experience in a comparable organization; a degree in museum studies, education, marketing, business or a related field is preferred.

Demonstrated success in nonprofit fundraising, donor development and securing significant philanthropic support.

Proven experience writing and securing grants from local, state and/or federal sources.

Experience developing or leading a capital campaign.

Strong financial management, organizational leadership and strategic planning skills.

Experience working effectively with nonprofit boards, committees, staff, volunteers and community stakeholders.

Working knowledge of museum operations and experience helping lead an organization through growth or transition.

Excellent communication, interpersonal and relationship\-building skills.

**Application Process**

**To apply:** Submit a cover letter, resume and three professional references with contact information to **president@flbm.org**.

**Application deadline:** October 15, 2026  
**Anticipated start date:** Negotiable

Learn more about the Finger Lakes Boating Museum at **flbm.org**.

Pay: From $65,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Health insurance
* Paid time off

Work Location: In person

**ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION**

Mackinac Island is one of Michigan's most iconic destinations — a community where horse\-drawn carriages and bicycles are the only transportation and Victorian architecture meets the pristine waters of Lake Huron. The Mackinac Island Convention \& Visitors Bureau (MICVB) promotes the island to visitors, advances the tourism industry through state and federal advocacy, and serves the local business community through the Mackinac Island Tourism Bureau.

The MICVB operates with four full\-time and four seasonal staff, and manages relationships with a state lobbying firm, federal lobbying firm, PR firm, and digital advertising agency. The ED also oversees the MITB\-PAC — a federal Political Action Committee advocating for H\-2B Visa reform — and represents the island on statewide travel and tourism boards.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

The MICVB Board of Directors seeks an exceptional leader to serve as its next Executive Director. This is a rare opportunity to lead a high\-profile destination organization on one of America's most storied islands — stewarding a beloved brand, championing the island's interests in Lansing and Washington, D.C., and serving the vibrant business community that makes Mackinac Island extraordinary.

The next ED will inherit a strong organizational foundation, established advocacy relationships, and deep community goodwill — with the opportunity to shape the bureau's next chapter, deepen member engagement, and ensure Mackinac Island remains a world\-class destination for generations to come.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Organizational Leadership**

* Serve as chief executive of the MICVB, Mackinac Island Tourism Bureau, and MITB\-PAC
* Lead and develop a team of four full\-time and four seasonal staff
* Report to the Board of Directors on performance, strategy, and financial health
* Manage contracts with the state and federal lobbying firms, PR firm, and digital advertising agency

**Destination Marketing \& Brand**

* Oversee brand strategy and positioning of Mackinac Island as a premier travel destination
* Direct advertising, PR, content, and social media programs that drive visitation and overnight stays
* Manage visitor information booth operations
* Lead event programming that animates the destination and generates media attention

**Advocacy \& Government Relations**

* Lead state\-level advocacy with the Michigan Legislature and state agencies
* Direct federal advocacy through the island's D.C. lobbying firm and MITB\-PAC
* Represent Mackinac Island on statewide travel and tourism boards and coalitions
* Cultivate relationships with elected officials and policy stakeholders at all levels

**Mackinac Island Tourism Bureau \& Member Engagement**

* Lead the Mackinac Island Tourism Bureau — the island's chamber of commerce — overseeing member recruitment, retention, and programming
* Serve as a trusted resource and advocate for the local business community
* Foster collaboration across tourism, retail, hospitality, and civic stakeholders

**Finance \& Administration**

* Develop and manage the annual budget across all three entities
* Pursue grants, sponsorships, and revenue diversification opportunities
* Ensure compliance with all nonprofit, Tourism Bureau, and MITB\-PAC regulatory requirements

**QUALIFICATIONS \& REQUIREMENTS**

**Required**

* Minimum 5 years of experience in tourism, destination marketing, DMO management, hospitality, or a related field
* Proven ability to lead a small professional team, including seasonal staff
* Experience overseeing marketing, advertising, PR, or brand programs
* Strong relationship\-building skills with the ability to represent the organization at government, industry, and community levels
* Experience managing vendor or agency relationships (advertising, PR, lobbying, or similar)
* Financial management experience including budget development in a nonprofit or association setting
* Seasonal island residency required — executive housing on Mackinac Island is provided with a portion of costs subsidized by the employer
* Ability to travel as needed for advocacy, conferences, and industry events

**Preferred**

* Experience in government relations or advocacy at the state or federal level
* Familiarity with PAC administration, compliance, and H\-2B Visa workforce policy
* Experience in a seasonal, island, or resort destination market
* Existing relationships with Michigan tourism stakeholders and/or elected officials
* Bachelor's degree in marketing, communications, public administration, or business; graduate degree a plus
* Fluency in digital advertising, social media strategy, and content marketing

**COMPENSATION \& BENEFITS**

**Salary**

Commensurate with experience; competitive with the scope of this role

**Health Insurance**

Comprehensive health insurance provided

**Retirement**

401(k) retirement plan

**Residency \& Housing**

Access to executive housing on Mackinac Island with a portion of costs subsidized by the employer

**Remote Work**

Remote work opportunities available during the off\-season

**Vacation \& Leave**

Comprehensive vacation and leave policies

Support for industry conferences and continuing education

The Lansdowne Economic Development Corporation (LEDC) seeks an Executive Director (ED). The LEDC is a 501(c)(3\) not\-for\-profit organization whose mission is to promote a responsive local economy that invites our entire community to support the arts, local businesses, and public spaces and events. The LEDC envisions an inviting, connected, and vibrant Lansdowne where the entire community celebrates arts, culture, and local business. The organization currently pursues the overarching goals of making Lansdowne a regional arts and culture destination that celebrates our local communities; a place where artists, businesses, and residents connect to strengthen a shared sense of place and belonging; and promoting community well\-being, healthy living, and improving residents’ quality of life.

The Executive Director is the chief administrative officer responsible for leading the LEDC in achieving its mission and implementing the LEDC’s policies and strategic vision as defined by the Board of Directors.

The desired candidate will have a deep understanding of non\-profit strategy and small business needs, along with a proven ability to think strategically and lead effectively.

Major functions of the Executive Director include staff management and recruitment, managing fundraising and finances, and community\-building and coordination.

**Background** 

Lansdowne Pennsylvania is a diverse and vibrant creative community six miles from Philadelphia City Hall. Lansdowne boasts a walkable downtown with excellent public transportation including bus, trolley, and regional rail connecting to Philadelphia, Media, and the Main Line; we are a short 13\-minute ride to University City by train. Lansdowne has a large concentration of Victorian\-era homes, with two National Historic Districts. Housing is affordable and there is a strong sense of community and volunteerism. Lansdowne has traditionally been home to artists, small creative businesses, and residents involved in higher education.

Lansdowne is currently experiencing a rejuvenation. The Historic Lansdowne Theater, shuttered for thirty\-five years, has successfully undergone a jaw\-dropping restoration and is entertaining 1200\-capacity audiences regularly. Exciting new businesses are moving in. Traffic is increasing. Excitement around our maker space classes and events is palpable. The LEDC is poised to leverage our town’s many diverse assets to facilitate further growth of our human\-based economy.

**Responsibilities**

*Administrative*

* Report regularly to the LEDC Board on financial, administrative, human resources, committee, and community matters.
* Work with the LEDC Board, staff, and volunteers to define and implement the strategic goals and objectives of the LEDC.
* Oversee staff, including performance reviews, payroll, and benefits administration; manage consultants.
* Maintain official records and ensure compliance with regulations and funding source requirements.
* Coordinate economic development and revitalization programs, including analysis and monitoring, business development, and business recruitment.
* Identify, attract, and work with prospective traditional businesses as well as small businesses including makers and artists.

*Governance*

* Prepare materials for and attend all meetings of the Board of Directors.
* Assist the Board and Committees to fulfill governance objectives.
* Recruit, hire, supervise and evaluate LEDC staff, interns and consultants; serve as an interface between the Board and staff.
* Manage and attend Committee meetings and keep committee members apprised of ongoing activities and projects.
* Assist Committees in the administrative planning and execution of major events, including the annual Arts Festival, holiday art show, Juneteenth, and farmers markets.

*Fundraising and Finance*

* Oversee the LEDC fundraising plan and implementation, including research and cultivation of potential funding sources, apply for grants, and carry out corporate sponsor and individual donor programs.
* Prepare and provide all required reports for grants received.
* Work with the staff, Board, and Committees in developing the annual budget; manage the budget.
* Monitor revenues and expenditures in relation to the budget; report regularly to the Board.
* Manage billing and receiving and approve payroll disbursements.

*Community*

* Identify and foster collaboration between stakeholders in the community, including the Borough’s staff, Council and Mayor, the Lansdowne Business Association, community organizations and individuals, and independent businesses.
* Identify talent in the community and recruit volunteers and staff.
* Attend Borough meetings as needed.
* Recruit new businesses and provide ongoing support to help them achieve success in Lansdowne.

**Qualifications**

* A minimum of 5 years of demonstrated staff and budget management experience.
* Proven strong leadership, with demonstrated planning, organizational, and entrepreneurial abilities.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Successful experience researching grant opportunities, writing grant proposals, grant administration, and close\-out.
* Bachelor’s degree in community development, urban planning, urban studies, historic preservation, non\-profit or public administration, arts administration, or a related field is preferred. Higher education is desired.
* Previous work experience with state agencies in community redevelopment is a plus.

**Compensation**

The LEDC Executive Director position is non\-exempt. The salary range is $70,000\-$85,000 with a negotiable stipend towards health coverage.

The LEDC offers paid time off for holidays, sick days and vacation.

**Job Summary**

We are seeking a dynamic and strategic Chief Operating Officer (COO) to lead our organization’s operational functions and drive sustainable growth. As a key member of the executive leadership team, the COO will oversee business operations, implement operational excellence initiatives, and foster a culture of continuous improvement. This role demands a proactive leader with exceptional management skills, strategic vision, and a passion for optimizing processes to achieve organizational goals. The ideal candidate will excel in managing large\-scale organizational change, developing innovative business strategies, and ensuring operational efficiency across all departments.

**Duties**

* Lead the development and execution of strategic plans to advance operational efficiency and organizational growth.
* Oversee daily business operations, ensuring alignment with company objectives and industry best practices.
* Drive operational excellence initiatives by implementing process improvements, quality standards, and performance metrics.
* Manage business development efforts to identify new opportunities, expand market presence, and foster client relationships.
* Supervise senior leadership teams across departments, promoting collaboration and accountability.
* Develop and manage budgets, forecasts, and financial plans to ensure fiscal responsibility and profitability.
* Lead large\-scale organizational change management projects to adapt to evolving market conditions and internal growth strategies.
* Utilize data\-driven decision\-making techniques to analyze operational performance and inform strategic initiatives.
* Oversee project management efforts ensuring timely delivery within scope and budget constraints.
* Conduct profit and loss analysis to optimize revenue streams and control costs effectively.
* Foster a culture of continuous improvement by encouraging innovation, teamwork, and leadership development at all levels.

**Qualifications**

* Proven experience in senior leadership roles with a focus on operations management and strategic planning.
* Demonstrated success in leading operational excellence initiatives and large\-scale organizational change management projects.
* Strong background in business development management, financial management, budgeting, forecasting, and profit \& loss analysis.
* Expertise in process improvement methodologies such as Lean or Six Sigma is highly desirable.
* Excellent verbal communication skills with the ability to engage effectively with executives, stakeholders, and teams at all levels.
* Experience managing cross\-functional teams with supervising responsibilities across multiple departments or regions.
* Proficiency in data analysis tools and data\-driven decision\-making processes.
* Knowledge of project management principles with a track record of delivering complex programs on time and within budget.
* Ability to lead change management initiatives confidently while maintaining high levels of team engagement.
* Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Management or related field; advanced degrees or certifications are preferred.

**Hansel Union Consulting: Chief Clinical Officer Job Description**

**An introduction to Hansel Union**

Hansel Union is a market leader in providing holistic therapeutic services to children, adults and families with developmental, intellectual, and neurological disabilities. 80% of HUCO clients are autistic adults. We pride ourselves on offering a comprehensive suite of therapy support services integrating behavioral, speech\-language, recreational, physical and occupational therapies as well as psychology.

**Overview**

The Chief Clinical Officer is the senior clinical leader of Hansel Union, holding accountability for the quality, safety, and clinical integrity of all therapeutic services across every discipline and market served. Through oversight of clinical standards, governance, and the development of the clinical team, the Chief Clinical Officer ensures that the care delivered to clients and their families reflects the highest professional, ethical, and regulatory standards.

The Chief Clinical Officer reports to the Chief Executive Officer and works in close partnership with the President, who holds operational, administrative, and financial accountability. This partnership aligns clinical excellence with organizational performance so that HUCO can deliver consistent, high\-quality therapeutic services as it grows.

Acting on behalf of the organization, the Chief Clinical Officer holds responsibility for clinical governance, standards of care, and the professional oversight of all clinical staff and discipline leads, in alignment with HUCO's mission, vision, guiding principles, and applicable acts, regulations, and standards of practice.

The Chief Clinical Officer provides clinical leadership to the Board, clinical staff, and discipline leads in developing HUCO's therapeutic model, treatment philosophy, and service lines in line with current clinical evidence, best practice, and the needs of the communities served.

A knowledgeable, credible, and collaborative clinical leader, the Chief Clinical Officer builds on the organization's standard of clinical excellence, identifies opportunities to strengthen and expand services, and ensures that clinical resources and talent are aligned with present and future goals. The Veteran Advocacy Project (VAP) is seeking an attorney to serve as Deputy Executive Director.
  

This individual will work closely with the Executive Director in guiding the organization's next

maintaining the values that shape our work. The Deputy Executive Director will help lead
  

organizational strategy, program direction, partnerships, and fundraising.

families, with a focus on those living with post\-traumatic stress, brain injury, substance dependency,
  

and other mental health conditions. Through advocacy, education, and free legal services, the team
  

fights for clients' rights to benefits, keeps families in their homes, and empowers veterans by
  

removing barriers to recovery and success.
  

  

We are partnered with VA Vet centers, community health clinics, and veterans' organizations to
  

reach individuals where they are. While our attorneys tackle the legal challenges, our advocates
  

connect clients to culturally competent, trauma\-informed resources. VAP helps veterans and their
  

families achieve the stability needed to regain their health and rebuild their lives.
  

  

The Deputy Executive Director will help shape organizational priorities, strengthen partnerships, and
  

support thoughtful growth. The role will include supervision of the civil legal services team,

new_jobs.description:
The Lansdowne Economic Development Corporation (LEDC) seeks an Executive Director (ED). The LEDC is a 501(c)(3\) not\-for\-profit organization whose mission is to promote a responsive local economy that invites our entire community to support the arts, local businesses, and public spaces and events. The LEDC envisions an inviting, connected, and vibrant Lansdowne where the entire community celebrates arts, culture, and local business. The organization currently pursues the overarching goals of making Lansdowne a regional arts and culture destination that celebrates our local communities; a place where artists, businesses, and residents connect to strengthen a shared sense of place and belonging; and promoting community well\-being, healthy living, and improving residents’ quality of life.

The Executive Director is the chief administrative officer responsible for leading the LEDC in achieving its mission and implementing the LEDC’s policies and strategic vision as defined by the Board of Directors.

The desired candidate will have a deep understanding of non\-profit strategy and small business needs, along with a proven ability to think strategically and lead effectively.

Major functions of the Executive Director include staff management and recruitment, managing fundraising and finances, and community\-building and coordination.

**Background** 

Lansdowne Pennsylvania is a diverse and vibrant creative community six miles from Philadelphia City Hall. Lansdowne boasts a walkable downtown with excellent public transportation including bus, trolley, and regional rail connecting to Philadelphia, Media, and the Main Line; we are a short 13\-minute ride to University City by train. Lansdowne has a large concentration of Victorian\-era homes, with two National Historic Districts. Housing is affordable and there is a strong sense of community and volunteerism. Lansdowne has traditionally been home to artists, small creative businesses, and residents involved in higher education.

Lansdowne is currently experiencing a rejuvenation. The Historic Lansdowne Theater, shuttered for thirty\-five years, has successfully undergone a jaw\-dropping restoration and is entertaining 1200\-capacity audiences regularly. Exciting new businesses are moving in. Traffic is increasing. Excitement around our maker space classes and events is palpable. The LEDC is poised to leverage our town’s many diverse assets to facilitate further growth of our human\-based economy.

**Responsibilities**

*Administrative*

* Report regularly to the LEDC Board on financial, administrative, human resources, committee, and community matters.
* Work with the LEDC Board, staff, and volunteers to define and implement the strategic goals and objectives of the LEDC.
* Oversee staff, including performance reviews, payroll, and benefits administration; manage consultants.
* Maintain official records and ensure compliance with regulations and funding source requirements.
* Coordinate economic development and revitalization programs, including analysis and monitoring, business development, and business recruitment.
* Identify, attract, and work with prospective traditional businesses as well as small businesses including makers and artists.

*Governance*

* Prepare materials for and attend all meetings of the Board of Directors.
* Assist the Board and Committees to fulfill governance objectives.
* Recruit, hire, supervise and evaluate LEDC staff, interns and consultants; serve as an interface between the Board and staff.
* Manage and attend Committee meetings and keep committee members apprised of ongoing activities and projects.
* Assist Committees in the administrative planning and execution of major events, including the annual Arts Festival, holiday art show, Juneteenth, and farmers markets.

*Fundraising and Finance*

* Oversee the LEDC fundraising plan and implementation, including research and cultivation of potential funding sources, apply for grants, and carry out corporate sponsor and individual donor programs.
* Prepare and provide all required reports for grants received.
* Work with the staff, Board, and Committees in developing the annual budget; manage the budget.
* Monitor revenues and expenditures in relation to the budget; report regularly to the Board.
* Manage billing and receiving and approve payroll disbursements.

*Community*

* Identify and foster collaboration between stakeholders in the community, including the Borough’s staff, Council and Mayor, the Lansdowne Business Association, community organizations and individuals, and independent businesses.
* Identify talent in the community and recruit volunteers and staff.
* Attend Borough meetings as needed.
* Recruit new businesses and provide ongoing support to help them achieve success in Lansdowne.

**Qualifications**

* A minimum of 5 years of demonstrated staff and budget management experience.
* Proven strong leadership, with demonstrated planning, organizational, and entrepreneurial abilities.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Successful experience researching grant opportunities, writing grant proposals, grant administration, and close\-out.
* Bachelor’s degree in community development, urban planning, urban studies, historic preservation, non\-profit or public administration, arts administration, or a related field is preferred. Higher education is desired.
* Previous work experience with state agencies in community redevelopment is a plus.

**Compensation**

The LEDC Executive Director position is non\-exempt. The salary range is $70,000\-$85,000 with a negotiable stipend towards health coverage.

The LEDC offers paid time off for holidays, sick days and vacation.

**Application Information**

The LEDC is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national orig
